# Aruna

> Aruna is a type-safe networking framework for roblox-ts. You define server actions
> (client → server RPC) and signals (server → client push) once, in TypeScript, with
> schemas; the `aruna build` compiler generates typed client/server stubs, a runtime,
> and a Rojo-buildable project layout. This file is written for coding agents: it
> describes the public API and the things that are easy to get wrong.

## What you are looking at

You are reading this from inside `node_modules/@arunajs/aruna`. This is a published
library. Consumer code imports from four runtime entry points and three generated
virtual modules:

- `aruna/server`  — `defineAction`, `defineSignal`, `createServerApp`, dispatch/validation
- `aruna/client`  — `createClientApp` (argless default transport; can own the signal subscriber via `{ signals, createSubscriber }`), `invokeAction`
- `aruna/roblox`  — the RemoteEvent server transport (`robloxRemoteEvent` for `createServerApp({ transport })`), `createActionInvoker`, low-level `bindActions`, signal pub/sub
- `aruna/schema`  — `schema.*` builders + `Infer` (the single schema-inference type)
- `$aruna/actions/server` — generated server action registry (`actions`, `defaultRateLimit`)
- `$aruna/actions/client` — generated per-action client call functions
- `$aruna/signals` — generated signal registry (`signals`)

The `aruna/*` and `$aruna/*` specifiers are tsconfig path aliases written by
`aruna build` / `aruna doctor --fix`. They are NOT the npm subpath exports
(`@arunajs/aruna/server`); in a real project you import the short `aruna/*` form.

## Docs

- [Getting started](./docs/getting-started.md): install, project shape, the build loop, a full minimal action round-trip.
- [Actions](./docs/actions.md): `defineAction`, server registration, client calls, rate limits, fire-and-forget, `ctx.player`, `ctx.publisher`.
- [Signals](./docs/signals.md): `defineSignal`, server publisher (`to`/`toMany`/`toAll`), client subscriber, publishing from inside an action (`ctx.publisher` / `createActionDefiner`).
- [Stores](./docs/stores.md): `defineStore` / `definePlayerStore`, `StoreResult` error taxonomy, session locking, migrations, `createServerApp({ playerStore })` and `ctx.store`.
- [Schema](./docs/schema.md): every `schema.*` builder, numeric width hints, Roblox userdata (vector3/color3/cframe), inference.
- [CLI](./docs/cli.md): `aruna build`/`check`/`init`/`doctor`/`inspect`/`contract`, flags, what each generates.
- [Architecture](./docs/architecture.md): module boundaries, the client/server/shared partition, generated modules, the dual runtime, binary codec.

## Rules of thumb (read before writing Aruna code)

- Stores are server-only persistence. A failed load NEVER falls back to the default —
  that is how a save file gets overwritten. Handle `{ ok: false }` explicitly, and treat an
  absent `ctx.store` as "not loaded", not "new player". See stores.md.
- Action and signal definitions are discovered by file classification (client/server/shared
  by path convention). Server-only logic must live in server-classified files or the
  compiler reports a boundary violation. See architecture.md.
- Concerns have a file form and a folder form: `actions.ts` or `actions/`, `ui.tsx` or
  `ui/`, and so on. Definitions are found by their `define*` call, so split a concern
  across as many files as you want — no config change, no naming ceremony.
- A domain (`src/domains/<name>/`) keeps its `client/` and `server/` subtrees private.
  Other domains may import its root modules — or only its `index.ts` once it has one —
  and reaching past that reports `aruna::304`. Same-domain and app-shell imports are
  unrestricted. See architecture.md.
- After adding or changing any `defineAction`/`defineSignal`, run `aruna build` — `aruna check`
  does NOT regenerate stubs or the manifest, so client stubs go stale.
- `ctx.player` is always present (wire dispatches carry the caller; in-process
  `app.dispatch` requires a ctx with a player). Import `defineAction` from
  `aruna/roblox` to get `ctx.player: Player` typing. Test actions through
  `createServerApp(...).dispatch(actionId, { player }, input)`.
- To publish a signal from inside an action, use `ctx.publisher` (injected when
  `createServerApp` owns a publisher). Bind `createActionDefiner<Signals, Player>()`
  in a shared module for a non-optional, registry-checked `ctx.publisher`.
- If `aruna check` reports `aruna::110`/`aruna::111` (stale artifact / alias desync),
  run `aruna build` (prunes stale output) and `aruna doctor --fix --emit-runtime`
  (realigns tsconfig aliases). Generated output under `generatedDir` is fully owned.
- Schemas are plain immutable objects with zero runtime cost; compose by spreading
  `.shape`, never mutate.
